items.title: Concept
items.text: OS Tuning involves optimizing operating system parameters, resources, and configurations to maximize database performance. The OS is the foundation layer that provides CPU, memory, I/O, and network resources to the database.

items.title: On-Premises
items.text: Direct control over kernel parameters, system resources, and hardware configurations. Requires coordination between DBA, System Admin, and Storage teams.

items.title: Cloud (AWS RDS)
items.text: Managed service with limited OS access. Optimization through instance classes, parameter groups, and storage types. Provider handles kernel-level tuning.

codeExamples.title: Check Application Logs
codeExamples.code:
# Review application error logs
tail -f /var/log/application/app.log | grep -i "slow\|timeout\|error"

# Check for specific slow query patterns
grep "execution time" /var/log/application/app.log | awk '{if($NF>1000)print}'

codeExamples.title: Quick Database Connection Test
codeExamples.code:
# Test database connectivity and response time
time psql -h prod-db-01 -U dbuser -d production -c "SELECT 1;"

# Check active connections
psql -h prod-db-01 -U dbuser -d production -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;"

steps.title: ANALYZE
steps.details: Use top, vmstat, iostat, free -m, sysctl -a

codeExamples.title: System Resource Analysis
codeExamples.code:
# Check CPU and memory usage
top -b -n 1 | head -20

# Memory statistics
free -m

# Check swap usage (high swap = memory pressure)
vmstat 1 5

codeExamples.title: I/O Performance Check
codeExamples.code:
# Disk I/O statistics
iostat -x 2 5

# Check for I/O wait
sar -u 1 10

# Identify processes causing I/O
iotop -o -b -n 3

codeExamples.title: Identify Memory Bottleneck
codeExamples.code:
# Check current shared memory limits
ipcs -lm

# Output shows:
# max seg size (kbytes) = 32768  # Only 32MB!

# Check what PostgreSQL is requesting
grep shared_buffers /etc/postgresql/14/main/postgresql.conf

codeExamples.title: Calculate Required Memory
codeExamples.code:
# Server has 64GB RAM
# PostgreSQL best practice: 25% for shared_buffers
# Required: 64GB * 0.25 = 16GB

# Convert to bytes for shmmax
echo "16 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024" | bc
# Result: 17179869184

# Convert to pages for shmall (page size = 4096)
echo "17179869184 / 4096" | bc
# Result: 4194304
